notes: The two הוּא tokens take the copulas the ASV writes for them. The competing reading — rule 20's tripartite sentence, leaving them unrepresented and handing the copula to the predicate — fails here because each predicate is a finite relative clause that already carries its own predication, so no predicate morpheme is available to bear a second English verb.
אֵין with כָּל shares the single *no* under rule 35, the presentative frame joining the existential and the unit heading on the negation (rule 50).
חָדָשׁ takes *new thing*, headed on the word carrying the lexeme (rule 31).
